key_insight: Thermal buoyancy strongly reshapes phototactic bioconvection, lowering the critical bioconvection threshold and driving a transition from phototaxis-dominated instability to thermally driven convection.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and control onset, mode, and amplitude of microorganism-driven flows in heated or cooled suspensions relevant to bioengineering and thermal-fluid systems.
method: Linear stability analysis to compute critical onset conditions.
Solved direct and adjoint eigenvalue problems plus a second-order resolvent system.
Derived a Stuart-Landau amplitude equation to classify nonlinear bifurcations and finite-amplitude behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical evaluation over varying thermal Rayleigh numbers, showing the critical bioconvection Rayleigh number tends to zero near the classical Rayleigh-Bénard threshold and that the Landau coefficient is positive.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on weakly nonlinear theory near onset, so predictions may be less reliable far from critical conditions or in strongly nonlinear regimes.
paper_title: Weakly Nonlinear Analysis of Phototactic Bioconvection under Thermal Buoyancy
